name: Bradford protein assay
description: Coomassie dye binds protein and shifts its absorbance to 595 nm. Typical microplate format: 5 µl of standard or sample plus 250 µl of dye reagent, 10 minutes at room temperature. Follow your reagent supplier's instructions for volumes and timing.

name: BCA protein assay
description: Protein reduces Cu²⁺ to Cu⁺, which forms a purple complex with bicinchoninic acid (562 nm). Typical microplate format: 25 µl of standard or sample plus 200 µl of working reagent, 30 minutes at 37 °C. Follow your kit's instructions.

name: Lowry protein assay
description: Alkaline copper treatment followed by the Folin–Ciocalteu reagent gives a blue colour read at 750 nm (the top of the SpectraMax 250 range). Typical incubation is 30 minutes at room temperature after adding the Folin reagent. Follow your kit's instructions.

name: ELISA (TMB, 450 nm)
description: Read after adding acid stop solution to the TMB substrate. The reduction subtracts the 650 nm reading (plate imperfections, scratches) from the 450 nm signal: L1−L2.

name: Kinetic enzyme assay (Vmax)
description: Reads every 20 seconds for 10 minutes and reports Vmax, the steepest slope, in mOD/min. 405 nm suits p-nitrophenol products (for example from pNPP); change the wavelength for other chromophores (340 nm for NADH, read as a decrease).

name: Michaelis-Menten (Km, Vmax)
description: Each well gets a different substrate concentration. The plate is read kinetically and each well's Vmax becomes one point of the substrate curve; the graph fits v = Vmax·[S]/(Km + [S]).
